study type: Cross-sectional analysis within a cohort study
exposure: Molecular allergology patterns (s-IgE levels to specific molecules)
outcome: Sensitization to food extract allergens (egg, milk, peanut, wheat)
Sensitization to specific food allergen molecules (ovomucoid, casein, Ara h 1-3, omega-5-gliadin)
cohort: The study included 1110 3-month-old infants from the Scandinavian antenatally recruited PreventADALL mother-child cohort.
finding: At 3 months of age, 7.3% of infants showed specific sensitization, predominantly to food allergens often without detectable s-IgE to specific molecules, and maternal food sensitization was significantly associated with infant sensitization.
